title.narrative: EU FPI SGBV Referral Pathways in Sudan

description.narrative: GOAL and Christian Aid (CA) are proposing an action to expand services and spaces for women to prevent and respond to sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV), and to increase the inclusion and influence of women in peace building forums. In doing so, the action aims to improve the safety and protection of women in targeted areas of North Darfur (ND) and South Kordofan (SK) states. To achieve this, GOAL and CA will focus on building local knowledge, capacities, networks, and infrastructure of local actors. They will leverage existing GOAL partnerships and programs that support health services and referrals for sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) survivors and apply an "ecological model" along with proven social behaviour change (SBC) approaches to alter attitudes and promote women's access to influential spaces. The design is organized under three mutually-reinforcing outcomes: Output 1 will improve comprehensive services for survivors and girls and women at risk of SGBV, Output 2 is to improve upholding of girls’ and women’s rights in the targeted areas, Output 3 will advance women’s inclusion and influence in local decision-making and peacebuilding forums. GOAL and CA will work according to an 18-month timeframe, working deliberately and step-by-step to facilitate sustainable changes. The transition of these outputs to clear impact on women will depend on several assumptions holding, including that authorities continue to formally register and allow the work of these organizations, that the target population from an area are not displaced or significantly disrupted by direct fighting or severe famine in the area, that community leaders and local authorities have a basic willingness to engage, and that women's groups themselves remain engaged and motivated throughout the project timeframe despite the challenges they face.
